messages:
claire (devex): Quick one — our onboarding sample throws at edge with 'Unexpected token export' referencing a subpath import like @ourorg/lib/foo. Local pnpm workspace run fine. anyone seen subpath + exports + hoist symlink issues?
ishaan (eng-runtime): yep. subpath imports are fragile if package.exports uses a wildcard that points to cjs. bundlers for edge expect ESM; if exports doesn't provide an 'import' conditional for subpaths, the optimizer can pull a CJS file.
viv (pkg-team): our lib mutated a few months ago; we only published an esm bundle for top-level "./" but left subpaths mapping to cjs via a wildcard. pasted exports (redacted):
```json
"exports": {
  "./*": "./dist/cjs/*",
  ".": "./dist/esm/index.js",
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
ishaan (eng-runtime): that's exactly it — wildcard forces subpaths to the cjs build. For subpath imports you either need matching import/require conditionals for "./*" or avoid exposing subpaths and force consumers to use the root entry.
ara (ts): types caveat: TS in a workspace resolves through source so editors aren't warning. But when consumers install from registry the published d.ts must sit next to the exported ESM file for subpath imports to type-check. If your types point to types/index.d.ts but you publish dist/esm/foo.d.ts, TS resolution can fail.
claire (devex): ok — two questions: 1) quick fix to unblock sample? 2) longer-term guardrails?
viv (pkg-team): 1) quick fix: republish a tiny patch that adds conditional exports for subpaths:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" },
  "./*": { "import": "./dist/esm/*", "require": "./dist/cjs/*" },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
That ensures import-based resolvers pick ESM for both root and subpaths.
ishaan (eng-runtime): app-side workaround if you can't republish immediately: configure bundler/optimizer to prefer module/import fields. For webpack/rollup set mainFields: ['exports','module','main'] and ensure esbuild target is ESM. But that's brittle — fix upstream.
ara (ts): 2) guardrails: add a CI pack check that runs npm pack and verifies dist/esm exists for root and relevant subpaths, and that types files are adjacent (e.g., dist/esm/foo.d.ts). Also add a prepublish script asserting exports has import conditional.
pack-bot: running pack-check for @ourorg/lib@0.7.3... tar contents: dist/esm/index.js present; dist/esm/foo.js missing -> FAIL.
viv (pkg-team): thanks pack-bot — found the missing build step that skipped per-file esm artifacts. patching build and republishing now.
claire (devex): redeploying sample after republish. i'll add a short note in the quickstart README explaining why local workspace runs may not catch publish-time subpath/export issues.
ishaan (eng-runtime): one extra note — pnpm hoist layout can hide missing files locally because installing from workspace uses symlinks to project source. Tools like Yarn PnP are stricter and will surface this earlier. CI pack-check and real install-from-tgz smoke tests are the best safety net.
viv (pkg-team): republished — pack-check passed. redeploy green. adding prepublish CI job and PR checklist: ensure esm per-subpath, conditional exports, types adjacent, and tarball verification.
claire (devex): perfect. i'll post a short tip summary in #devex for package owners. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
